content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-7821 fired: `network-lb-health` (severity: P1). Auto-page to #incidents and on-call rotation.

pagerduty: Incident triggered by 5xx spike from edge -> backend TLS handshake failures, threshold exceeded 5m.

alice: acked. I'm the current on-call, looking. Any initial impact numbers?

samir: seeing alert graphs — us-east-1 front doors show 15% 5xx over 2m, error type = TLS alert (handshake_failure).

rita: confirmed from Synthetics: curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health returns TLS handshake aborted intermittently.

infra-sre: ran a quick ELB check:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --query 'TargetHealthDescriptions[*].{Id:Target.Id,State:TargetHealth.State,Reason:TargetHealth.Reason}'
```
Results: 3/8 targets UNHEALTHY (TLS timeout) in us-east-1-pool-a.

maria: also saw high connection resets between ALB and application nodes; logs show `SSL_do_handshake() failed` with `alert handshake_failure` from s2n.

alice: possible recent cert rotation? Who pushed certs in last 60m?

eng-plat: we rotated leaf certs via cert-rotator job ~45m ago for us-east. Job reported success but that could be a partial rollout.

rita: DNS check: `dig api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8 +short` -> returns multiple A records; TTL shows 300, but some upstream caches still serve old IPs. Could be partial DNS propagation + new cert not on old IPs.

samir: this smells like mix of (1) partial cert rollout, (2) LB still routing to old hosts without new cert, (3) TLS mismatch when client SNI expects new cert.

alice: customer impact: initial estimate ~12% of requests in us-east failing with 5xx. APAC and EU less affected. Notify support to surface to customers?

alice: support-alerts, please post to status page that we're investigating network/TLS errors impacting a subset of users in us-east.

oncall-bot: @alice, don't forget to run the incident checklist: set bridge, assign severity, track updates.

alice: creating bridge now -> https://meet.example.com/redwood-incident-PD7821. Joining.

infra-sre: quick mitigation options:
- rollback cert roll to previous version for us-east pool (if we have it ready)
- temporarily mark unhealthy targets and drain traffic to standby pool (failover)
- change ALB health check to HTTP endpoint (non-TLS) to keep targets in service while we debug TLS

samir: I can flip the target group to direct traffic to us-east-standby which still has the old certs. That will drop latency but should restore success rate. Any objections?

rita: +1 for standby failover, prefer not to rollback certs mid-deploy. Standby will buy time and reduce customer impact.

alice: do it. samir, coordinate with infra-sre and eng-plat for DNS implications. Notify me when traffic starts shifting.

eng-plat: executing failover now. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn ... --default-actions TargetGroupArn=arn:...-standby`

infra-sre: switching target group routing -> standby. Health checks show standby targets healthy.

samir: traffic shift in progress: 40% -> 100% within next 30s. Monitoring...

rita: quick synthetic check after 60s: curl -> 200 OK, TLS negotiated with cert CN=api.redwood.example.com (issuer Let's Encrypt). No handshake errors observed.

alice: nice. 5xx rate dropped from 15% to 1.2% in us-east. Customer impact reduced.

maria: while traffic is stable, we should root-cause cert-rotator behavior: logs show successful push to a subset of hosts but 3 nodes failed to accept new cert due to short-lived race around keystore reload.

eng-plat: confirmed. The rollout job did a rolling restart but the keystore reload path had a bug when concurrent restarts happened; some nodes served old certs, others the new. Mixed certs + DNS cached IPs -> TLS mismatch.

alice: action items (short):
- oncall (alice) maintain bridge and updates to status page.
- eng-plat (samir, rita) pause cert-rotator rollout and patch keystore reload logic.
- infra-sre (maria) evaluate automation to fail fast on partial rollout (detect handshake error spikes).
- support: notify customers already impacted and add note to status page.

samir: I'll open an urgent PR to add a keystore-reload retry + better health gating for cert rollout. ETA 2h for patch + canary.

rita: for immediate safety, we should increase TTL for the standby pool DNS to avoid rapid flips, and lower it for the primary in next maintenance to prevent long-lived caches next time.

alice: agreed. Also request post-incident follow-up to update runbooks: add explicit failover steps and certificate rollout health checks.

oncall-bot: paging handoff scheduled in 30m. Who will take second shift?

eng-plat: I'll take handoff at +30m (samir). Leave bridge and notes.

alice: handing off to @samir in 30m. For now, keep monitoring for 1h.

pagerduty: Incident PD-7821 acknowledged by alice at 2771234569. Escalation suppressed due to ack. If condition persists >15m, auto-escalate to secondary.

alice: final update for channel: mitigated via traffic failover to standby targets; partial customer impact reduced. Root cause: partial cert rollout + keystore reload race causing TLS handshake failures. Next steps being tracked in internal ticket ENG-1129.

maria: creating postmortem skeleton and will attach logs/traces and timeline.

samir: will revert traffic back after patch + canary validation. Will post when ready.

alice: closing channel updates for now. If anything regresses, re-open thread or page oncall. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: PD-7821 status -> acknowledged, mitigation in place, monitoring.
